messages.content: Write a customer case study about a company that adopted a continuous delivery platform and now deploys more often. Around 250 words.

# Kettlebridge Freight: from fortnightly release nights to forty deploys a week

Kettlebridge Freight had a release ritual. Every other Thursday, twelve engineers stayed late, a change-approval board signed off on a spreadsheet, and someone watched dashboards until midnight. Deploys were rare, so each one carried three weeks of accumulated changes. When something broke, nobody could say which of the 400 commits did it.

They moved to a continuous delivery platform in March 2024. The migration took a quarter, and most of that quarter went into things that had nothing to do with the platform: splitting a shared database, writing the first real integration tests the billing service ever had, and getting the security team comfortable with automated approval for low-risk changes.

The numbers eighteen months on: 22 deploys per quarter became roughly 40 per week. Lead time from merge to production dropped from eleven days to under four hours. Change failure rate went from 14 percent to 3. Rollbacks take 90 seconds and no longer require a phone call.

"The honest version is that we didn't get faster because the tool is fast," says Priya Raghunathan, who ran the migration. "We got faster because deploying stopped being an event. When you ship twenty times a day, a bad deploy is a Tuesday afternoon, not an incident."

Kettlebridge still has a change-approval board. It reviews schema migrations and anything touching payment routing, which is about one change in forty. Everything else goes out when the pipeline is green.

The on-call rotation is quieter, too. Last quarter it paged nine times.

---
